data.title: Reflections on Sudoku, or the Impossibility of Systematizing Thought
data.author: rjpower9000
data.article_summary:
本文反思了在解决编程问题（如数独求解器）时的思维过程，并联系到**Entscheidungsproblem**（决策问题）。作者讨论了在编程和写作中面临的挑战，即如何在动手编码或写作前充分思考问题空间，而不至于过早陷入细节。作者提出了“10%规则”，即在开始编码前花10%的时间思考问题，以避免过早迷失方向。

作者进一步探讨了是否能系统化思维过程，提到即便像陶哲轩这样的数学家也无法解决所有问题。他得出结论，思维无法完全系统化，每个人依赖不同的思维工具，且这些工具可通过学习改进。

文章还比较了**Ron Jeffries**和**Peter Norvig**在数独求解器开发中的不同方法。Jeffries采用测试驱动开发（TDD），但过程冗长且效果不佳；Norvig则通过高层次分析和有效数据结构，迅速找到解决方案。作者认为Norvig的方法更系统，但他也承认Norvig在相关领域有丰富经验。

最终，作者对TDD持保留态度，认为测试无法解决“知道该做什么”的根本问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程设计方法的有效性及思考过程，特别是关于测试驱动开发（TDD）和设计的关系。

不同观点：
• **支持深度思考和设计优先**：[mbb70] 引用了 Rich Hickey 的“Hammock Driven Development”演讲，主张通过深入思考和研究他人的经验来设计解决方案，认为好的设计不会自然地从编程中产生，背景知识和领域知识至关重要。

• **TDD的局限性**：[JonChesterfield] 和 [schoen] 讨论了TDD的局限性，尤其是当问题从简单起点到解决方案的路径不是平滑可微时，TDD的效果会受到限制。此外，[schoen] 指出，软件的正确性通常是突变的，而不是渐变的，这使得通过迭代改进找到正确的程序变得困难。

• **认知风格和方法的个性化**：[awanderingmind] 认为文章对不同编程方法的分析很少泛化，具体分析了不同方法在特定领域中的不足，并暗示这些方法可能反映了不同的认知风格。

• **AI和人类思维的不可替代性**：[prmph] 提到AI无法系统化人类思维，特别是在解决一般智力挑战方面，即使是创建CRUD应用，也无法完全自动化和标准化。

• **流行与非流行技术的有效性**：[taeric] 指出，有些流行技术确实在某些领域有更好的成功率，但一些不受欢迎的技术也可能比我们愿意承认的更有效。

补充讨论：
• [fydorm] 提到偶然读到Norvig关于Sudoku的文章，显示出讨论的主题在社区中引起了关注。
• [IceDane] 对Ron Jeffries文章表示不满，认为其教条主义不奏效，暗示对某些TDD倡导者的观点持批评态度。

争议焦点：
• TDD是否在所有情况下都有效，特别是在复杂问题和算法问题中，是否能通过迭代改进找到正确的解决方案。
• 编程设计中深度思考和背景知识的重要性与依赖TDD等技术方法之间的平衡。

44220245.article_content:
Reflections on Sudoku, Or the Impossibility of Systematizing Thought
I reflect on the Entscheidungsproblem how it relates to Sudoku solvers. It's a little weird.
.
The other day, to no one's surprise, I was fumbling over a programming problem.
This wasn't anything satisfyingly algorithmic, but more the thing where you're
evaluating a million questions on "how should I structure this system?". While
I'm no design purist, I like to at least make an attempt at sketching out the
problem space and think through options before I just start coding something. My
rule of thumb for this is, let's call it the "10% rule" - make sure I try to
think hard about a problem for 10% of the time before I start playing around
with code. Writing code helps clarify many things but it's also easy to get
stuck in local minima
I have the same problem when writing text, like this blog post. Put me in front of an editor and I'll pointlessly recraft sentences instead of getting the thing finished.
. This rule helps keep me from getting lost too early,
but I often think about whether I could do better.
I'd like to say I have a systematic process I apply here. I don't. I think
over one idea, then another,
writing down my thoughts
,
but it's always hard to feel like you're making a lot of progress.
It's honestly frustrating. I often wish I could "systematize" it somehow,
applying some rigorous method and march towards the solution. Could I become one of
those
magic people
who just sit down in front of a problem and watch it decompose in front
of them?
Over time I've accepted that is impossible. There is no person, no process,
which can systematize thought. Millions of math problems
elude
Terence Tao
despite his brilliance.
Now I see these differences in aptitude as having different sets of
mental tools at your disposal. The more tools you have, the better tools you
have, and the better you are at applying them, then the better you get at
certain problems. Maybe your background makes you better or more interested in
different tools. But we can all learn new tools, and get better at the ones we
have.
This is all kind of murky and unsatisfying though. Wouldn't it be nice if you
just had a general method you could apply to solve everything? What happens if
you
think
you have a method to solve all problems?
The Sudoku Affair
A few months ago I read Zach Tellman's fascinating article on the
Sudoku
Affair
, in which he revisited Peter Norvig & Ron
Jeffries very, very different attempts to produce a workable Sudoku solver. (I
highly recommend reading the original article as well, as Zach's deep analysis
of Ron Jeffries attempts at producing a Sudoku solver is fascinating).
Some background: Ron Jeffries made a career advocating for test-driven
development (TDD) and extreme programming. Peter Norvig is a research lead at
Google and author of many papers and a few books on AI. As you'd expect, this
leads to different approaches to problems.
Ron Jeffries attempted to solve Sudoku by approaching it
"rigorously"
No offense intended, but just being clear this isn't like
mathematical rigour
but more of an applied philosophy.
from the perspective of TDD. He outlines the
problem, writes a test case and begins to iterate, adding tests and refactoring.
In the initial set of posts, he can't get to a real solution despite many hours
of effort. He then revisited the problem 20 years later, and in the end spends
50
posts
writing about the process of building a solver. At some point, he
finds code from another site
and starts to bring that into the fold. He eventually gets to a solution, though at
that point I honestly have trouble figuring out how much TDD had to do with the process.
Peter Norvig takes a different approach, analyzing the high-level problem and
then breaking down the data structures and outlining the solution in the course
of ~20 lines of code. While his code might be a bit dense to follow initially,
the way he approaches the problem and pre-builds data structures makes "testing"
trivial. His test for validity is part of the search condition for his program.
It's hard not to appreciate the systematic nature of Peter's approach: define
the problem, look through your toolkit, apply the relevant tools, success. Of
course, Peter has an advantage that he's
written
books
about related techniques.
Ron Jeffries attempt definitely didn't make me excited about TDD, I at least
respected that he didn't try to hide things after the fact.
Many people have commented about this over time, with lots to say
about TDD and programming. In Peter Siebel's post on
Unit testing in Coders at Work
even Peter Norvig chimes in, indicating he's not "anti-test", but that tests don't fix the
underlying issue of "knowing what to do."
Then bloggers were arguing back and forth about what this means. I don’t think
it means much of anything—I think test-driven design is great. I do that a lot
more than I used to do. But you can test all you want and if you don’t know how

data.title: The Centralization of the Internet
data.author: vishnumohandas
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了互联网从去中心化向中心化转变的过程及其影响。最初，互联网是一个由相互连接的独立网络组成的分布式系统，没有中央控制机构，这种设计使其能够快速全球扩展且难以被单一国家关闭。然而，近十年来，互联网逐渐走向中心化，内容和数据越来越多地集中在谷歌、亚马逊、微软和Facebook等少数大公司手中。这一变化由规模经济驱动，包括“良性循环”、 impatience、基础设施成本和复杂性等因素，且受到政府政策的支持。中心化使这些大公司能够收集大量用户数据，建立更精准的预测模型，从而增强其经济实力和影响力。文章呼吁政府和商业领袖关注这一趋势及其潜在影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府是否应提供互联网服务给公民

不同观点：
• 观点一：政府已经悄然退出为公民提供互联网服务的角色。  
  - 论据：[fithisux]指出，过去政府在提供公共服务方面扮演重要角色，但现在似乎在互联网服务提供上缺位。  
  - 例子：未提及具体例子，但暗示政府过去曾参与电信、广播等公共服务。

• 观点二：私营企业更适合提供互联网服务。  
  - 论据：一些潜在的支持者认为，私营企业由于市场竞争和创新驱动，能够更有效地提供高质量的互联网服务。  
  - 例子：私营企业通过技术进步和投资，提高了互联网的速度和覆盖范围。

• 观点三：政府应在互联网服务中扮演更积极的角色。  
  - 论据：有些人认为互联网是现代社会的重要基础设施，政府有责任确保所有公民都能获得可负担的互联网服务。  
  - 例子：一些国家（如一些北欧国家）由政府主导，确保偏远地区也能获得良好的互联网服务。

• 观点四：政府和私营企业应合作提供互联网服务。  
  - 论据：部分人认为政府和私营企业的合作可以结合两者的优势，确保互联网服务的广泛覆盖和质量提升。  
  - 例子：通过公私合作项目，政府提供基础设施或补贴，私营企业负责运营和维护。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于政府是否应在互联网服务提供中承担责任。支持政府介入者强调公平和服务普及，支持私营企业者则强调效率和创新。  
- 另一个值得注意的点是，不同国家和地区的政府在互联网服务提供中的角色和策略可能不同，因此讨论具有地域性差异。

44254511.article_content:
The term
“internetwork”
originally described a set of interconnected networks—a network of networks. The global
Internet,
the largest and best-known computer network, is no different—it is a network of networks. Because the Internet is a network of networks,
no one owns the Internet.
Each network that makes up the Internet is owned and operated by a private company, college, government, or other organization.
The composition of the Internet—a network of independently owned networks—is not an accident. The design of each Internet component is intentionally tuned to support a
distributed
system, a network without a central controlling authority. The distributed nature of the Internet allowed it to spread quickly across the globe and makes it hard to “shut down the Internet” at any national border.
Recently, however—within the last ten years—the Internet has been moving toward centralization. Rather than dispersing data and services throughout the world, content and connectivity are being concentrated into a small set of hands. This centralization is causing many in the engineering and Internet policy world to become worried.
It’s time for leaders in government and business to notice what is happening to the global Internet.
It’s time for leaders in government and business to notice what is happening to the global Internet.

Public Discourse
Sign up and get our daily essays sent straight to your inbox.
Subscribe
The Centralization Process
In the original, decentralized Internet, most communication was directly between computers. When your computer accesses a website, it’s accessing a set of files on some other computer.
Where
that other computer is physically located isn’t all that important to the way the network works—so long as there is some physical path between the two computers, content can be transferred.
As the Internet grew, companies began to specialize in hosting (or creating) content, carrying (or transiting) data, or providing access to the Internet (edge providers), as shown in the figure below.
Transit providers specialize in carrying traffic between cities, nations, and continents using specialized long-haul optical fiber cables. These cables run just about everywhere. Most of the Internet traffic between continents (and sometimes between different places on the same continent) runs through undersea optical links.
However, in the last ten years or so, content providers—particularly social media and cloud computing companies—
have moved into the Internet core.
The result is an infrastructure that looks closer to the illustration below.
Most of the Internet’s traffic now flows through the networks of a few large companies, like Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Facebook, rather than through transit providers. The Internet’s physical infrastructure is being reshaped to meet this new reality. Much as landscapers put sidewalks where the grass dies, network operators put physical links and infrastructure where the traffic flows.
The Information Cycle
Why
is this centralization happening? It’s primarily a result of economies of scale, which have several elements. The “virtuous cycle,” impatience, the cost of infrastructure, and complexity all play a role in the increasing centralization of the Internet. Many of these are bolstered by specific government and inter-governmental policies.
According to
Kai-Fu Lee,
a prominent artificial intelligence researcher and author of the book
AI Superpowers: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order
,
information about people using a service is bound into a “virtuous cycle.” Readers of
Public Discourse
may object to calling this cycle of information, analytics, and consuming ever more attention “virtuous,” since it does not promote
virtue
in the classical sense. From the perspective of the AI developer and data scientist, however, the cycle can be considered “virtuous” because it gathers more information, allowing more precise and predictive models to be built.
The more information you have about people, the more information you can feed your machine-learning process to build detailed profiles about your users. Understanding your users means you can predict what they will like, what they will emotionally engage with, and what will make them act. The more you can engage users, the longer they will use your service, enabling you to gather more information about them. Knowing what makes your users act allows you to convert views into purchases, increasing the provider’s economic power.
The virtuous cycle is related to the network effect. The value of a network is exponentially related to the number of people connected to the network. The value of the network increases as more people connect, because the information held within the network increases as more people connect.
Who will extract the value of those data?

“Anonymity is a shield from the tyranny of the majority,” wrote Supreme Court Justice John Paul Stevens in a 1995
ruling
affirming Americans’ constitutional right to engage in anonymous political speech.
That shield has weakened in recent years due to advances in the surveillance technology available to law enforcement. What used to be a manual process is becoming increasingly automated, making mass deanonymization of protesters, even those taking active steps to hide their identities, possible.
Controversies about facial recognition and
masking
may
dominate the news
, but there are a plethora of surveillance methods that law enforcement can deploy to gain insight into peoples’ identities, communications, and purchases. Almost everyone in modern life, and that includes protesters, continuously oozes data that reveals sensitive aspects of their life. Everything from social media posts, to metadata about phone calls, to the purchase information collected by data brokers, to location data showing every step taken, is available to law enforcement — often without a warrant.
Check out our
investigation
into how these digital data trails complicate politicians’ efforts to prohibit protesters from wearing masks at public demonstrations.
Incoming President Trump has sworn that he will pursue various groups like his political enemies or immigrants, and
could use
the expansion of the national surveillance state for his own purposes.
Avoiding all of this tracking would require such extrication from modern social life that it would be virtually impossible for most people. That said, some simple steps could help in not becoming the lowest hanging fruit, like leaving a cell phone behind. Understanding more about what technologies the local police force has access to can also inform how a community approaches surveillance and safety issues.
Here are just some of the technologies law enforcement can use to surveil protesters.
Stingrays (a.k.a. IMSI Catchers or Cell Site Simulators)
What is it?
International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) catchers, or Stingrays, impersonate cell phone towers to collect the unique ID of a cell phone’s SIM card. These IDs allow law enforcement officials to request additional information from phone carriers, matching devices with owners’ names, addresses, and location histories.
Stingrays help law enforcement to collect data even
without a warrant
. Since the technology has the capability to collect information about all the phones in an area, it's an ideal method for identifying people en masse.
While some cities, like New York, have published
guidelines
on how IMSI catchers can be deployed, others have been less forthcoming — even
lying to judges
to conceal their use of the technology.
Who sells it?
The name “Stingray” is the name of a specific device made by
L3Harris
(formerly known as Harris), but has now colloquially become the generic term for all cell site simulators. IMSI catchers are sold by
many other companies
, like
Digital Receiver Technology
.
Can it be circumvented?
Apple and Google
, which control the operating systems of nearly all smartphones in the U.S., have begun preventing cell phones from dropping down from more advanced and protected network protocols, like 5G, to less secure 2G networks, which are necessary for IMSI catchers to function.
Protesters are also often advised to either put their phones on airplane mode, which shuts down any cellular connections, or just leave their devices at home.
Some groups are trying to develop workarounds to allow phone communication at protests without the need to connect to a cellular network — although
research
suggests that sort of mesh network communication may not be the most secure either.
Tushar Jois, a City College of New York computer science professor studying privacy, is working on one such app called
Amigo
. He recommends using end-to-end encrypted chat messaging platforms (like
Signal
), encrypting the data on your phone and
in the cloud
, as well as enabling settings like Apple’s Lockdown Mode, which enhances the device’s security. Still, nothing beats leaving the phone at home.
Geofencing
What is it?
Geofence warrants, also known as reverse location warrants, are a type of search warrant that lets law enforcement
request location data from apps on your phone or tech companies,
about all the devices or users in a certain area within a specified time frame. Geofence warrants are being increasingly used on
protesters
, with evidence of the technique being deployed to identify people
demonstrating
against the police shooting of Jacob Blake in Kenosha, Wisconsin and the students who
marched
in protest of a statue of a Confederate soldier on the campus of the University of North Carolina.

data.title: It's the end of observability as we know it (and I feel fine)
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary: 文章《It’s The End Of Observability As We Know It (And I Feel Fine)》讨论了大型语言模型（LLMs）在可观察性工具领域的颠覆性影响。作者Austin Parker指出，LLMs作为通用函数逼近器，能够有效分析和解决系统中的问题，例如通过自动化工具调查性能异常。文章描述了作者使用LLM代理结合Honeycomb的Model Context Protocol（MCP）服务器，在80秒内以低成本分析出前端服务延迟峰值的根本原因。这一示例表明，LLMs可以自动化并取代传统的可观察性分析工作，从而改变系统设计和运维方式。作者强调，随着LLMs分析成本的下降和OpenTelemetry的普及，传统的可观察性工具面临巨大挑战，行业需要重新思考其价值主张。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在可观察性（observability）和SRE（站点可靠性工程）领域的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• **[RainyDayTmrw]** 认为集体上低估了确定性（determinism）的价值，同时高估了非确定性（nondeterminism）的成本。他们提到了一款尝试通过关联图表分析事件的产品，但结果往往是荒谬和错误的，类似于[spurious correlations](https://tylervigen.com/spurious-correlations)。

• **[zug_zug]** 担心工具在10%的情况下会得出错误结论，且没有公开承认其不确定性，导致团队成员错误使用工具，从而引发更多问题。建议工具应首先得出结论，然后寻找数据反驳该结论，并公开其不确定性。

• **[heinrichhartman]** 对OpenTelemetry历史描述提出异议，认为Honeycomb并非如文章所说引领了OpenTelemetry的发展。OpenTelemetry是由OpenCensus和OpenTracing合并而来，且最初由Google和LightStep等组织主导。

• **[stego-tech]** 认为LLM在可观察性领域的应用对小型和中型企业（SMBs和SMEs）特别有价值，因为这些企业缺乏资金和专家来实现复杂的监控和可观察性部署。LLM可以帮助这些企业以更低的成本实现高级别的监控。

• **[nilkn]** 认为LLM不会彻底终结可观察性，但它们确实会逐渐在SRE领域发挥更大的作用。然而，现有的可观察性技术栈仍将不可或缺，特别是在LLM的幻觉、可靠性和信任问题尚未解决的情况下。

• **[resonious]** 认为文章标题过于戏剧化。现有的可观察性工具仍然必不可少，LLM只是帮助人们更快地完成已经掌握的任务，并不会彻底取代任何特定技能。

• **[geraneum]** 质疑LLM工具是否能够泛化应用。认为即使LLM在演示中表现良好，也需要证明其在非训练数据上的泛化能力，才能宣布可观察性的终结。

• **[gilbetron]** 指出LLM在失败时仍需要人类介入，且数据收集和存储的复杂性依然存在。可观察性的“终结”可能意味着文化的深刻转变，而不仅仅是技术变革。

• **[yellow_lead]** 对文章宣称的“AI带来可观察性的终结”持怀疑态度，认为这种说法过于夸张。

• **[ok_dad]** 讽刺地评论说，利用AI做人类专家可以做的事情是一种“好”的商业策略，但实际上对大多数AI应用公司都适用。

• **[Kiyo-Lynn]** 分享了个人经验，表示随着系统复杂性增加，传统的仪表板和警报变得难以处理，而AI可以帮助快速找到线索，但同时也担心过度依赖AI会削弱人类的判断和分析能力。

• **[kacesensitive]** 认为LLM不会取代可观察性，但会改变游戏规则。快速获得根本原因分析的能力非常有价值，但仍需要良好的遥测数据支持。

• **[vanschelven]** 认为如果系统复杂性需要借助AI来解开，那么这个系统设计可能存在问题。隐藏复杂性并不等于抽象，好的系统设计应该本身就是可观察的。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到LLM在失败情况下的不确定性和可靠性问题，强调人类监督的必要性。
• 对OpenTelemetry历史解读的不同意见反映出对技术发展历程的不同看法。
• 多个评论提到LLM对小型企业和复杂系统的潜在价值，但也对其泛化能力和文化影响持谨慎态度。

争议焦点：
• LLM是否能够真正替代或显著改变现有的可观察性和SRE工作流程。
• 对OpenTelemetry等技术发展历史的不同解读。
• LLM工具的可靠性和不确定性问题如何解决。

August 23rd, 2024
8 Best Practices to Understand and Build Generative AI Applications Effectively
Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is making waves across various industries, promising to revolutionize how we handle data and automate complex tasks. Learn to navigate the technical hurdles, hype, and ethical concerns.
LEARN MORE
In a really broad sense, the history of observability tools over the past couple of decades have been about a pretty simple concept: how do we make terabytes of heterogeneous telemetry data comprehensible to human beings? New Relic did this for the Rails revolution, Datadog did it for the rise of AWS, and Honeycomb led the way for
OpenTelemetry
.
The loop has been the same in each case. New abstractions and techniques for software development and deployment gain traction, those abstractions make software more accessible by hiding complexity, and that complexity requires new ways to monitor and measure what’s happening. We build tools like dashboards, adaptive alerting, and dynamic sampling. All of these help us compress the sheer amount of
stuff
happening into something that’s comprehensible to our human intelligence.
In AI, I see the death of this paradigm. It’s already real, it’s already here, and it’s going to fundamentally change the way we approach systems design and operation in the future.
New to Honeycomb? Get your
free
account today.
TRY NOW
LLMs are just universal function approximators, but it turns out that those are really useful
I’m going to tell you a story. It’s about this picture:
If you’ve ever seen a Honeycomb demo, you’ve probably seen this image. We love it, because it’s not only a great way to show a real-world problem—it’s something that plays well to our core strengths of enabling investigatory loops. Those little peaks you see in the heatmap represent slow requests in a
frontend
service that rise over time before suddenly resetting. They represent a small percentage of your users experiencing poor performance—and we all know what this means in the real world: lost sales, poor experience, and general malaise at the continued enshittification of software.
In a Honeycomb demo, we show you how easy it is to use our UI to understand what those spikes actually mean. You draw a box around them, and we run
BubbleUp
to detect anomalies by analyzing the trace data that’s backing this visualization, showing you what’s similar and what’s different between the spikes and the baseline. Eventually, you can drill down to the specific service and even method call that’s causing the problem. It’s a great demo, and it really shows the power of our platform.
Last Friday, I showed a demo at our weekly internal Demo Day. It started with what I just showed you, and then I ran a single prompt through an AI agent that read as follows:
Please investigate the odd latency spikes in the frontend service that happen every four hours or so, and tell me why they’re happening.
The screenshot here elides the remainder of the response from the LLM (please find the entire text at the end of this post), but there’s a few things I want to call out. First, this wasn’t anything too special. The agent was something I wrote myself in a couple of days; it’s just an LLM calling tools in a loop. The model itself is off-the-shelf
Claude Sonnet 4
. The integration with Honeycomb is our new
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
server. It took 80 seconds, made eight tool calls, and not only did it tell me why those spikes happened, it figured it out in a pretty similar manner to how we’d tell you to do it with BubbleUp.
This isn’t a contrived example. I basically asked the agent the same question we’d ask you in a demo, and the agent figured it out with no additional prompts, training, or guidance. It effectively zero-shot a real-world scenario.
And it did it for
sixty cents.
If I can do this, so can you. So can anyone.
I want to be clear, this was perhaps the
least
optimized version of this workflow. Inference costs are only going down, and we can certainly make our MCP server more efficient. There are ways to reduce the amount of input tokens even more. We can play around with more tailored aggregations and function calls that return LLM-optimized query results. It’s an exciting new era!
It also should serve as a wakeup call to the entire industry. This is a seismic shift in how we should conceptualize observability tooling.
If your product’s value proposition is nice graphs and easy instrumentation, you are
le cooked
.
An LLM commoditizes the analysis piece, OpenTelemetry commoditizes the instrumentation piece.
The moats are emptying.

• **[heinrichhartman]** 对OpenTelemetry历史描述提出异议，认为Honeycomb并非如文章所说引领了OpenTelemetry的发展。OpenTelemetry是由OpenCensus和OpenTracing合并而来，且最初由Google和LightStep等组织主导。

• **[stego-tech]** 认为LLM在可观察性领域的应用对小型和中型企业（SMBs和SMEs）特别有价值，因为这些企业缺乏资金和专家来实现复杂的监控和可观察性部署。LLM可以帮助这些企业以更低的成本实现高级别的监控。

• **[nilkn]** 认为LLM不会彻底终结可观察性，但它们确实会逐渐在SRE领域发挥更大的作用。然而，现有的可观察性技术栈仍将不可或缺，特别是在LLM的幻觉、可靠性和信任问题尚未解决的情况下。

• **[resonious]** 认为文章标题过于戏剧化。现有的可观察性工具仍然必不可少，LLM只是帮助人们更快地完成已经掌握的任务，并不会彻底取代任何特定技能。

• **[geraneum]** 质疑LLM工具是否能够泛化应用。认为即使LLM在演示中表现良好，也需要证明其在非训练数据上的泛化能力，才能宣布可观察性的终结。

• **[gilbetron]** 指出LLM在失败时仍需要人类介入，且数据收集和存储的复杂性依然存在。可观察性的“终结”可能意味着文化的深刻转变，而不仅仅是技术变革。

• **[yellow_lead]** 对文章宣称的“AI带来可观察性的终结”持怀疑态度，认为这种说法过于夸张。

• **[ok_dad]** 讽刺地评论说，利用AI做人类专家可以做的事情是一种“好”的商业策略，但实际上对大多数AI应用公司都适用。

• **[Kiyo-Lynn]** 分享了个人经验，表示随着系统复杂性增加，传统的仪表板和警报变得难以处理，而AI可以帮助快速找到线索，但同时也担心过度依赖AI会削弱人类的判断和分析能力。

• **[kacesensitive]** 认为LLM不会取代可观察性，但会改变游戏规则。快速获得根本原因分析的能力非常有价值，但仍需要良好的遥测数据支持。

• **[vanschelven]** 认为如果系统复杂性需要借助AI来解开，那么这个系统设计可能存在问题。隐藏复杂性并不等于抽象，好的系统设计应该本身就是可观察的。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到LLM在失败情况下的不确定性和可靠性问题，强调人类监督的必要性。
• 对OpenTelemetry历史解读的不同意见反映出对技术发展历程的不同看法。
• 多个评论提到LLM对小型企业和复杂系统的潜在价值，但也对其泛化能力和文化影响持谨慎态度。

争议焦点：
• LLM是否能够真正替代或显著改变现有的可观察性和SRE工作流程。
• 对OpenTelemetry等技术发展历史的不同解读。
• LLM工具的可靠性和不确定性问题如何解决。

data.title: Dubious Math in Infinite Jest (2009)
data.author: rafaepta
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了《无尽的玩笑》中出现的一些数学错误。作者Mike Strong是一位大卫·福斯特·华莱士的粉丝，他 initially 对这些错误并未在意，但在阅读了华莱士的其他作品和一篇数学小说评论后，重新燃起了对《无尽的玩笑》中数学错误的兴趣。作者记录了书中发现的四个错误，其中两个可能是印刷错误。这些错误包括叙述者对108场网球比赛以54-54平局结束的概率计算错误，以及角色Mike Pemulis误用积分中值定理来解释核武器分配。作者强调，这些错误并不影响作品的整体价值，只是对数学有兴趣的读者可能会觉得有趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大卫·福斯特·华莱士（David Foster Wallace）小说《无尽的玩笑》（Infinite Jest）中的数学错误是否是故意设置的，以及这些错误是否影响了对作品的理解。

不同观点：
• 一些读者如npilk认为，书中的数学错误可能是作者故意设置的，目的是反映角色Pemulis并没有他自己想象的那么聪明，或者这些错误只是编辑在90年代难以检查出来的疏漏。此外，有人提出Pemulis的角色与《哈姆雷特》中的Polonious相似，后者也是一个自认为聪明但经常犯错的角色。
• A_D_E_P_T指出，华莱士在另一部作品《Everything and More: A Compact History of Infinity》中也犯了许多数学错误，并认为这可能是由于华莱士自身的数学能力有限，特别是在涉及康托尔的无穷大概念时。
• andy_xor_andrew则以轻松的语气提出，Pemulis可能就是不擅长数学，因此犯了错误。
• nneonneo提供了一个详细的数学分析，说明书中的某些概率错误在实际计算中是可以理解的，虽然不精确但接近正确值，因此可能只是技术性失误。
• arh68提出多种可能性，包括这些错误可能是打字错误，或是角色故意为之，甚至暗示小说中的世界可能是一个数学规则不同的平行宇宙。

补充讨论：
• FL33TW00D表达了对《无尽的玩笑》的情感价值，认为即使有数学错误，这本书仍然具有情感吸引力。
• neuroelectron提到阅读《无尽的玩笑》的体验，认为其细节过多，语法笨重，阅读体验缓慢，并表示更喜欢《万有引力之虹》（Gravity's Rainbow）。
• trefoiled指出，小说中的法语错误也非常多，很多人认为这些错误是故意设置的，以反映角色的特点。
• NewsaHackO和lou1306则从不同角度讨论了Pemulis在小说中使用的数学理论，认为角色可能故意夸大自己的能力，而不是真的精通数学。
• 最后，ProllyInfamous对华莱士和另一位作家David Sedaris的整体文学价值提出质疑，认为他们的作品虽然阅读愉快，但缺乏深度，尤其在技术性知识方面显得不足。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于华莱士是否故意在书中设置数学错误以服务于角色的塑造，或者这些错误仅仅是作者的无心之失。读者对此有不同的解读，部分人认为错误反映了角色的局限性，而其他人则认为这可能只是编辑疏漏或作者自身知识不足所致。

Dubious Math in Infinite Jest
by
Mike Strong
Let me say, first of all, that I am a huge fan of David Foster Wallace in general and
Infinite Jest
in particular.
On my first reading of
IJ
, I noticed a few mathematical errors but thought little of them.
After reading the essay
Derivative Sport in Torndao Alley
in
A Supposedly Fun Thing I'll Never Do Again
, though, I became curious about why a writer with a clear aptitude for math would include such mistakes in his opus.
Therefore, during my second reading of
IJ
, I made a note of the errors that I noticed.
As it turned out, their number was smaller than I had imagined.
Consequently, I lost interest in this topic until reading DFW's review of a pair of mathematical novels in a scientific journal.
The broad knowledge of math demonstrated by DFW in this article rekindled my curiousity about the errors in
IJ
, and I decided to document them, in case others might be interested.
My list is actually quite short - only four
mistakes, two of which might well be typographical - and I offer no theories about why they appear.
One of the errors is attributable to the omniscient
narrator, while the other three are spoken
by Mike Pemulis.
Both, we can assume, are competent mathematicians.
Before I outline the errors, I must make a logistical note.
Because I am writing this using a simple text editor, I am somewhat symbolically challenged.
Exponentiation will be denoted using a caret (e.g., 2^3 = 8).
Also, I will not even attempt to depict an integral sign or the usual mathematical symbol for combinations, a pair of elongated parenthesis.
I hope this makes the explanations no less understandable.
The first, and perhaps the most interesting error that I noted, appears on page 259 of
IJ
.
The narrator states that the odds of a 108 game tennis match ending in a 54-match-all tie are 1 in 2^27.
This is incorrect by about seven orders of magnitude; in fact, such an outcome is much more likely than the narrator suggests.
The problem of determining the odds is an exercise in probabilty and combinatorics, a fancy mathematical term for systematic counting.
By the laws of probability, the odds of a 108 game match ending in a tie are
(the number of outcomes resulting in a 54-54 tie) / (the total number of possible outcomes).
The denominator in this expression is easy to calculate.
It is simply 2^108 (an example will follow).
The numerator can be found using the concept of combinations.
That is, the correct anwer is the total number of ways team A can be assigned exactly 54 victories out of the 108 matches.
(Of course, if team A wins exactly 54 matches, so must team B.)
In combinatorics this is referred to as "the number of combinations of 108 things taken 54 at a time."
Although the derivation is well beyond the scope of this discussion, it can be shown that the number of combinations of
n
things taken
m
at a time is
n! / ((n-m)! m!)
.
Therefore, the numerator in the probabilty expression above is 108! / (54! * 54!), and the correct odds are
(108! / (54! *54!))/(2^108) or approximately 0.0766.
This is considerably greater than 1/2^27, or about 0.00000000745.
To illustrate this result, consider the following enumerable example:
What are the odds of a 4 game match ending in a 2-2 tie?
Again, the method above predicts that odds are
(4! / (2! * 2!))/(2^4)
=
(24 / (2 * 2))/(16)
= 6/16.
The answer suggested by the narrator of
IJ
would be 1/(2^1) = 1/2.
To see which is correct, we can list all 16 possible outcomes as follows:
AAAA
ABAA
BAAA
BBAA
AAAB
ABAB
BAAB
BBAB
AABA
ABBA
BABA
BBBA
AABB
ABBB
BABB
BBBB
Clearly, there are six outcomes resulting in a 2-2 tie (AABB, ABAB, ABBA, BAAB, BABA, and BBAA), so the odds are, indeed, 6/16 as the method above predicts.
The second significant instance of dubious math in
IJ
occurs in a footnote on pages 1023 and 1024.
In this section Mike Pemulis describes to Hal how the Mean Value Theorem for integrals can be used to distribute megatons of thermonuclear weapons among Eschaton combatants.
The Mean Value Theorem for integrals states that, for a function
f(x)
that is continunous on the interval from
x = a
to
x = b
,
the integral from
a
to
b
of
f(x)dx = f(x')(b - a)
for some value
x'
between
a
and
b.
In effect, this theorem simply states that the area underneath the curve described by the function
f(x)
from
x = a
to
x = b
is exactly the same as the area of a rectangle whose width extends from
a
to
b
and whose height has a value of
f(x')
for some value
x'
between
a
and
b
.
Now, while Pemulis' description of the theorem is essential correct, the problem in this footnote is the way the theorem is supposedly applied.
Specifically, the Mean Value Theorem for integrals is a theoretical tool for proving the
existence
of this particular
x'.
It does not, however, offer any method of finding the
value
of
x'
.
Therefore, it is difficult to imagine how the Mean Value Theorem for integrals could be employed in Pemulis' Eschaton calculations.

data.title: A receipt printer cured my procrastination
data.author: laurieherault
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何通过理解电子游戏让人上瘾的机制来克服拖延症，从而提高专注力和生产力。作者注意到自己能长时间专注于游戏，但对日常任务如写邮件却容易拖延。通过研究游戏中的即时反馈和频繁的任务循环（游戏循环），作者发现将任务细分为微任务并增强反馈可以有效减少拖延。作者使用了一台热敏收据打印机打印出细分任务列表，每完成一项任务就获得即时反馈（如将完成的便签纸揉成团丢掉），从而提高了工作效率和专注度。这种方法帮助作者更好地管理时间和任务，解决了长期以来的拖延问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对拖延症和工作中的分心问题，以及使用各种工具和方法（如任务列表、 receipt打印机）来提高生产力。

不同观点：
• jvanderbot认为游戏等高刺激活动会让人更难专注于低刺激的工作任务，类似于不健康饮食会让人难以享受健康食物。他提出通过减少高刺激活动（如游戏）来重新发现工作中的乐趣，类似于"多巴胺饮食"的概念。
• dackle分享了一个由David MacIver设计的每日任务列表系统，该系统强调从零开始创建一个扁平化的任务列表，通过这种方式筛选出真正重要的任务。他认为这种方法有助于集中注意力和提高动机。
• bengale和whalee对使用热敏纸打印任务的管理方法提出了健康担忧，指出热敏纸中的化学物质（如BPA/BPS）可能对健康有害，建议使用无酚热敏纸。
• reverendsteveii分享了自己在健身中使用的类似系统，通过白板和任务跟踪来管理日常锻炼，并指出多重奖励循环可以增加动力和持续性。
• PaulHoule讲述了自己尝试使用热敏打印机管理任务的经历，虽然最终没有完全实现与JIRA的联动，但发现了这些打印机在其他方面的用途（如打印Pokémon角色）。
• dclowd9901提出了一种通过小行动（如早上整理床铺）来调整心态的方法，认为这种小行动能带来心理上的舒适和满足感。
• fidotron讨论了物理任务表示和数字任务表示之间的心理差异，并提出如果用户界面更加拟物化，是否可以减少对物理工具（如打印机）的需求。

• orangebread认为即使方法再好，如果没有基本的动机，任何方法都难以奏效。他指出这些方法假设了使用者有动机但缺乏方法，而实际情况可能恰恰相反。

• 评论者对使用物理工具（如热敏纸打印机）的健康风险表示关注，并提供了替代建议。
• 有争议的焦点在于高刺激活动对工作任务的影响程度，以及是否需要通过减少高刺激活动来提高工作专注力。

44256499.article_content:
A receipt printer cured my procrastination
How I can focus on my to-do list by understanding the science of video games
Why can I focus for hours on a game but procrastinate when writing an email? For over 20 years, I've tried everything to boost my productivity. I've read dozens of books and tested many methods. Nothing made a real difference. But I finally found a solution by understanding what makes video games addictive. And a thermal receipt printer will become the best investment of my life.
My fight against procrastination
I started my business when I was 21 (I'm now 39). I built custom apps and did consulting for accounting software, invoicing systems, and point-of-sale tools.
Procrastination has always been my biggest struggle. The only way I could get things done was by relying on stress, coming from clients or financial pressure. That worked for a while, but it cost me my health (I burned out) and my business (I went bankrupt).
I noticed that I have no problem spending hours fully focused on a video game. If I can focus on a game, then my brain must also be capable of focusing on other tasks. So I naturally started asking myself why it's so easy to get hooked by a game, and how I could apply that same effect to tasks I struggle to complete.
It turns out that many of the struggles I've had throughout my life are linked to ADHD (Attention Deficit Disorder). The goal of this article isn't to focus on ADHD, but it's important to mention. ADHD affects many people, often without them even knowing it, in various ways and at different levels.
Why video games hook us
To understand what makes a video game addictive, let's take first-person shooters (FPS) as an example. FPS games are among the most popular and addictive games.
An FPS is built around a simple loop:
Aim
→
Shoot
→
Hit
or
Miss
. This is the
game loop
. The outcome, hit or miss, is immediately shown through sounds or visuals. This immediate reaction is called
feedback
.
For a game to be addictive, the game loop must repeat frequently and give strong feedback. Imagine an FPS where you only meet an enemy every 30 minutes. That wouldn't be engaging. The loop must repeat quickly to keep you interested.
Feedback in FPS games has improved a lot over time. Early FPS games only showed a simple blood splash when you hit an enemy. Modern games provide much stronger feedback. Now, when you hit an enemy, you might see:
the crosshair briefly changes to confirm the hit
damage numbers pop up above the enemy
sound effects
enemy death animations
a progress bar filling up
a new skill unlocked
random reward
and more...
Note that a game can have several game loops. For example, there can be another loop for finding random equipment for your character. Feedback can also come from outside the main loop, such as loot boxes or side missions.
For a game loop to be addictive, other factors matter too. You need to personally enjoy the type of game, and the challenge must match your skill level. If it's too easy or too hard, you won't be hooked. There are dozens of other factors, unique to each player's personality and preferences.
When all these elements come together, each game loop gives you a small dose of dopamine and creates a state of
flow
. In this state, we're fully focused, we lose track of time, and it's easier to handle complex tasks.
One final point: Video games are
easy to start
. They require very little motivation or discipline to start playing.
Key Takeaways:
The game loop should repeat often.
Feedback from the loop should be strong.
Games are easy to start, even with low motivation.
How to apply the feedback loop to our tasks
Based on what we've just seen, our real-life
game loop
is made up of completing tasks and habits throughout the day.
Our first goal is to
repeat this game loop as many times as possible each day
. A simple solution is breaking tasks into smaller parts. Let's take an example everyone can relate to: cleaning the house. At first glance, you might break down "Clean the house" like this:
Clean the house
Clean the kitchen
Clean the office
Clean the bedroom
...
If these three tasks take about an hour, that's only three game loops. Another problem is starting a task. Cleaning your bedroom might take 20 minutes, which feels too long when you're not motivated. So you procrastinate.
My solution is breaking things down even further:
Clean the house
Kitchen
Wash dishes
Wipe down surfaces
Clean floor
Take out trash
Bathroom
Clean shower
Clean toilet
Clean sink and mirror
Clean floor
Bedroom
Air out the bed
Make the bed
Organize closet
Clean floor
The rule is simple: the more you procrastinate on a task, the more you should break it down into micro-tasks, even ones that take just 2 to 5 minutes in extreme cases.
How to improve feedback
Now that we have our game loop, we are going to boost the feedback. To do this, I recommend using sticky notes. Write each task on a sticky note. When you finish the task, crumple the note into a ball and throw it in

data.author: Gud
data.article_summary: 2025年6月12日，Air India从艾哈迈达巴德飞往伦敦盖特威克的AI171航班在起飞后不久坠毁，机上共有242人，包括169名印度人、53名英国人、7名葡萄牙人和1名加拿大人。事故发生在当地时间下午1:38，飞机坠入梅加尼纳加尔的一栋医生宿舍楼。印度总理称这起事故“令人心痛不已”，卫生部长表示“许多人遇难”。初步报告称至少有105人死亡，现场救援工作正在进行。艾哈迈达巴德机场目前已关闭，所有航班暂停。英国外交部已成立危机小组处理此事。事故原因尚在调查中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Air India 波音787事故的分析与推测

不同观点：
• JumpCrisscross认为，在事故发生初期应避免过早阅读和相信有关因果关系的推测，因为这些推测往往是不准确的，甚至会混淆最终的调查结果。
• brunohaid指出，现代喷气客机发生如此严重的事故必定是某些极为严重的问题所致，例如机械故障或外部因素如鸟击。同时，他认为初期推测是一种锻炼思维的方式，有助于培养应急反应能力。
• DanielleMolloy提供了社交媒体上的信息，提到有乘客在事故后上传了飞机内部的情况，并提到过去一年中发生了多起类似事故。
• decimalenough引用了Flightradar24的数据，说明飞机在起飞后迅速下降，并推测由于飞机满载燃料，生还者希望渺茫。
• calcifer提到去年波音公司一名工程师举报并要求停飞所有787梦幻客机，暗示此次事故可能与飞机本身的设计或维护问题有关。
• leetrout关注到 intersection departure（交叉离场）的问题，认为在大型重型飞机上进行这种操作是不明智的，并提到通常航空公司有标准操作程序（SOPs）限制此类操作。
• m4tthumphrey推测飞机可能失去了动力，导致了事故的发生。

• babushkaboi列出了此次航班机组人员的信息，呼吁对机组人员的辛勤工作表示感谢。

• ihuk认为这是波音787的首起全损事故，强调了其罕见性。

• 争议焦点之一在于初期事故推测的价值。JumpCrisscross认为初期推测可能混淆视听，而brunohaid则认为这是一种有价值的思维训练。

data.title: Dancing brainwaves: How sound reshapes your brain networks in real time
data.author: lentoutcry
data.article_summary: 一项由奥胡斯大学和牛津大学合作进行的研究发现，当人们听到持续的节奏或音乐时，大脑不仅被动接受声音，还会实时重组其内部网络。研究引入了一种名为FREQ-NESS的新型神经影像技术，能够通过独特频率识别和追踪大脑网络的活动。这种方法揭示了不同声音频率如何像波浪一样在大脑区域间传播，提供了对感知、注意力甚至意识的全新理解。该技术为精确脑图绘制打开了大门，可能革新基础神经科学、脑机接口和临床诊断。研究结果表明，大脑在响应声音时会进行动态重构，而不仅是简单反应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：音乐对大脑的影响及其在提升专注力、编码工作等任务中的作用

不同观点：
• [主观体验与音乐推荐] rubicon33和shironandonon_认为音乐具有魔力，可以激发情感、帮助专注和激发灵感。rubicon33推荐了一些电子音乐曲目，而shironandonon_则推荐了psytrance、goa mixes以及一些techno音乐，并指出不同类型的音乐在不同情境下的作用（如在疲惫时听techno，抑郁时听trance）。

• [音乐播放列表与专注] chrisweekly分享了自己的Spotify播放列表，强调无歌词且能提升专注和能量的音乐有助于进入"flowstate"和进行深度工作。

• [神经科学视角] some1else和robviren从神经科学角度出发，讨论音乐如何通过不同的声音重塑大脑网络。some1else指出不同声音可能导致不同神经元激活，而robviren则对音频"治疗"的效果持怀疑态度，认为其效果因人而异。

• [具体研究与实践] kator和skeledrew提到具体的文章和研究，并结合个人经验讨论音乐对专注力的影响。kator提供了相关文章链接，skeledrew分享了在大学时使用双声道节拍音频进行自我调节的经验。

• [技术与哲学讨论] bluechair对文章的高层次解释表示不满，希望有更详细的解释。_DeadFred_引用圣奥古斯丁的名言，强调音乐对灵魂的愉悦和时间的连接作用。quantadev则从哲学和技术角度出发，讨论了音乐与意识、量子波之间的关系。

补充讨论：
• b0a04gl对网页后缀".htm"的持久使用表示赞赏，认为其具有手工制作的感觉，保持了一贯的发布流程。
• swayvil提到声音可能是最接近真实现实的感知形式。

争议焦点：
• 音乐对大脑和专注力的实际效果是真实存在还是仅为安慰剂效应。robviren对此持怀疑态度，而skeledrew则基于个人经验支持音频调节的效果。

Every beep, tone and new sound you hear travels from the ear to registering in your brain. But what actually happens in your brain when you listen to a continuous stream of sounds? A new study from Aarhus University and University of Oxford published in
Advanced Science
reveals that the brain doesn't simply register sound: it dynamically reshapes its organization in real time, orchestrating a complex interplay of brainwaves in multiple networks.
The research, led by Dr. Mattia Rosso and Associate Professor Leonardo Bonetti at the Center for Music in the Brain, Aarhus University, in collaboration with the University of Oxford, introduces a novel neuroimaging method called
FREQ-NESS
-- Frequency-resolved Network Estimation via Source Separation. Using advanced algorithms, this method disentangles overlapping brain networks based on their dominant frequency. Once a network is identified by its unique frequency, the method can then trace how it propagates in space across the brain.
"We're used to thinking of brainwaves like fixed stations -- alpha, beta, gamma -- and of brain anatomy as a set of distinct regions," says Dr. Rosso. "But what we see with FREQ-NESS is much richer. It is long known that brain activity is organized through activity in different frequencies, tuned both internally and to the environment. Starting from this fundamental principle, we've designed a method that finds how each frequency is expressed across the brain."
Opens the door to precise brain mapping
The development of FREQ-NESS represents a major advance in how scientists can investigate the brain's large-scale dynamics. Unlike traditional methods that rely on predefined frequency bands or regions of interest, the data-driven approach maps the whole brain's internal organization with high spectral and spatial precision. And that opens new possibilities for basic neuroscience, brain-computer interfaces, and clinical diagnostics.
This study adds to a growing body of research exploring how the brain's rhythmic structure shapes everything from music cognition to general perception and attention, and altered states of consciousness.
"The brain doesn't just react: it reconfigures. And now we can see it," says Professor Leonardo Bonetti, co-author and neuroscientist at Center for Music in the Brain, Aarhus University, and at the Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing, University of Oxford. "This could change how we study brain responses to music and beyond, including consciousness, mind-wandering, and broader interactions with the external world."
A large-scale research program is now underway to build on this methodology, supported by an international network of neuroscientists. Due to the high reliability across experimental conditions and across datasets -- FREQ-NESS might also pave the way for individualized brain mapping, explains Professor Leonardo Bonetti.

data.title: Quantum Computation Lecture Notes (2022)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这些是彼得·肖尔（Peter Shor）于2022年秋季量子计算课程的讲义。讲义涵盖了量子计算的基础与历史、叠加原理、单位ary演化、布洛赫球、量子测量、张量积、量子门、量子 teleportation、密度矩阵、GHZ实验、量子光学、Deutsch-Jozsa算法、Simon算法、量子傅里叶变换、相位估计、因数分解算法、离散对数算法、Grover搜索算法及其最优性证明、哈密顿量模拟、量子纠错码（9-qubit和7-qubit Hamming码）、量子CSS码，以及BB84量子密钥分发协议及其安全性证明。第26讲笔记未完成，可能未来补充。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算（Quantum Computing, QC）的标准资源、实际应用、行业入门以及对量子计算的质疑和个人学习困难。

不同观点：
• [hedgehog0] 认为 De Wolf 的笔记（https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09415）是当前的标准之一，并且比《Quantum Computation and Quantum Information》这本书更现代化和更新。
• [mikestorrent] 指出，关于量子退火（quantum annealing）的讨论缺失，这是目前唯一可能在我们的有生之年大规模应用的量子计算形式。
• [ofjcihen] 表示对量子计算很感兴趣，并且已经阅读了《Quantum Computation and Quantum Information》，但困惑于如何将所学应用于行业，尤其是缺少相关资源和指导。
• [fogof] 对某次讲座的标题没有提到原创者的名字表示不满，认为这是不合适的。
• [polamolo] 开玩笑地表示自己似乎在经历“土拨鼠日”，暗示对类似讨论的重复性感到厌倦。
• [rvz] 对量子计算持怀疑态度，认为经过数十年的发展，量子计算除了 Shor 算法和一些实验外，尚未产生实际的应用价值，甚至还不如目前的GPU集群有效。

补充讨论：
• [m3kw9] 表达了自己在面对数学方程时的困惑，暗示量子计算的学习难度较大。
• [revskill] 提出了一个关于如何在研究上变得非常优秀的问题，虽然与主要讨论点无直接关系，但反映出对科研能力提升的关注。

争议焦点：
• 量子计算的实际应用价值以及是否值得继续投入时间和资源发展。  
• [rvz] 对量子计算持怀疑态度，认为目前没有产生实质性的成果，而 [hedgehog0] 和 [ofjcihen] 则认为现有的书籍和资源（如 De Wolf 的笔记和《Quantum Computation and Quantum Information》）是重要的学习材料，表明对量子计算仍有积极的兴趣和研究价值。

data.title: Maximizing Battery Storage Profits via High-Frequency Intraday Trading
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种针对电网规模电池储能系统的高频交易策略，以最大化其在连续日内电力市场的收益。该策略考虑了限价订单簿的动态、市场规则和技术参数，并通过动态规划近似方法实现，比精确的混合整数线性规划快2-3个数量级。对德国订单簿数据的回测显示，该策略比每小时或每分钟优化一次的策略分别增加58%和14%的收益。此外，通过参数化扩展，进一步提高了年度收益8.4%。研究结果强调了交易速度对收益的关键作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电池能量存储系统（BESS）在电力市场中的应用及其优化潜力

不同观点：
• **amluto**：认为电池不能同时充电和放电是一个不合理的限制，建议通过修改电源电子设备或控制算法，使电池在不影响电池本身的情况下消耗多余的电力，并利用电池的热管理系统提供服务。同时指出在电力价格偶尔为负的情况下，电池应具备自我放电的能力以避免过热，并建议优化算法应考虑这一点。
• **ic_fly2**：指出在一些欧洲市场，已经通过编程实现了这种电池操作，且在英国市场中，电池的收益率因对冲基金的介入而显著下降。还提到一些公司在专门从事这类交易。
• **jillesvangurp**：强调电池生产率的提升和电池在不同场景中的潜在应用，特别是电动汽车（EVs）在电网中的潜在作用。提到如果EVs能够贡献电力，将为电网提供大量备用电力。此外，提到电池价格下降和新技术（如钠离子电池）的应用前景。
• **b0a04gl**：对文中提到的优化方法持怀疑态度，认为其在现实市场中的应用有限，指出实际市场存在延迟、断开、价格滑点、队列延迟等问题，而文中的方法只是在内存中的静态数据集上进行优化。
• **adds68**：提到在英国，已经通过Octopus Energy的Kraken Flex系统实现了工业规模的应用。
• **dachworker**：质疑为何要将具有潜力的交易策略公开发表，而不是卖给对冲基金，或者这只是对行业已经在做的事情进行正式发表。
• **thelastgallon**：建议直接使用EVs作为能量存储设备，指出EVs大部分时间是闲置的，可以用于吸收过剩电力或在电力价格高时供应电力。
• **saltspork**：提到在澳大利亚，通过Amber Electric等零售商，居民用户可以享受5分钟的现货定价，电池通过套利可以快速回本。
• **julienb_sea**：指出能源过剩生产将成为基载发电机的严重问题，并提到特斯拉的Powerwall/Autobidder和Base Power等公司在进行相关的市场交易。
• **brilee**：引用一篇文章，认为大多数利用免费能源的应用其资本成本远超能源的潜在收益。
• **buu700**：建议开发一种软件，能够在EVs、Powerwall等设备上自动进行充电和放电以获取被动收入，类似于电力而非股票的算法交易。
• **mellow_observer**：认为通过分布式电源存储获取小额收入是一种有趣的解决方案，但担心在大规模应用时可能出现的同步问题、功率流问题或存储电力的大规模下降问题。
• **potatoicecoffee**：质疑为何在有多余电力时不去进行海水淡化而是浪费电力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于电池优化方法在现实市场中的可行性和有效性，以及在分布式电源存储大规模应用时可能出现的问题。
• 讨论中多次提到电动汽车在电网中的潜在作用，特别是在电力价格波动时通过套利获取收益的可能性。
• 提到了新技术（如钠离子电池）的应用前景和电池价格的下降趋势，这可能对未来电网储能解决方案产生重大影响。
• 实际应用中的市场问题（如延迟、价格滑点等）与理论优化方法之间的差距也是一个重要的讨论点。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Maximizing revenue for grid-scale battery energy storage systems in continuous intraday electricity markets requires strategies that are able to seize trading opportunities as soon as new information arrives. This paper introduces and evaluates an automated high-frequency trading strategy for battery energy storage systems trading on the intraday market for power while explicitly considering the dynamics of the limit order book, market rules, and technical parameters. The standard rolling intrinsic strategy is adapted for continuous intraday electricity markets and solved using a dynamic programming approximation that is two to three orders of magnitude faster than an exact mixed-integer linear programming solution. A detailed backtest over a full year of German order book data demonstrates that the proposed dynamic programming formulation does not reduce trading profits and enables the policy to react to every relevant order book update, enabling realistic rapid backtesting. Our results show the significant revenue potential of high-frequency trading: our policy earns 58% more than when re-optimizing only once every hour and 14% more than when re-optimizing once per minute, highlighting that profits critically depend on trading speed. Furthermore, we leverage the speed of our algorithm to train a parametric extension of the rolling intrinsic, increasing yearly revenue by 8.4% out of sample.

44255728.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种针对电网规模电池储能系统的高频交易策略，以最大化其在连续日内电力市场的收益。该策略考虑了限价订单簿的动态、市场规则和技术参数，并通过动态规划近似方法实现，比精确的混合整数线性规划快2-3个数量级。对德国订单簿数据的回测显示，该策略比每小时或每分钟优化一次的策略分别增加58%和14%的收益。此外，通过参数化扩展，进一步提高了年度收益8.4%。研究结果强调了交易速度对收益的关键作用。

data.title: Pentagon Has Been Pushing Americans to Believe in UFOs for Decades, New Report
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了美国政府如何故意传播有关UFO（不明飞行物）的虚假信息，以转移公众对秘密武器计划的注意力。根据《华尔街日报》的报道和五角大楼设立的异常现象处理办公室（AARO）负责人肖恩·柯克帕特里克的调查，政府多年来通过伪造外星科技证据，助长了UFO神话。例如，1967年一个核掩体的UFO目击事件实际上是由军方测试电磁脉冲设备引起的，而非外星人活动。此外，一些新加入高度机密项目的军官还被展示虚假的UFO照片，作为某种“入会仪式”。这些发现揭示了UFO故事背后更世俗的解释，表明许多UFO传言可能是政府为掩盖国家安全秘密而制造的假象。

UFOs have been back in the news a lot lately, and it may be the case that the government wants it that way. Last week, the Wall Street Journal published the first of a two-part series that probes the ways in which the Defense Department has been responsible for creating and fostering the UFO mythology in America.
The article shows that the government has, at various points over the years, purposefully sown disinformation about UFOs, in an effort to make Americans believe in little green men. This news comes as the result of an internal investigation by Sean Kirkpatrick, the head of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), which was specifically set up within the Pentagon to investigate UFO sightings. Kirkpatrick, who spoke with the Journal, says he’s found evidence that the government “fabricated evidence of alien technology” in an effort to distract from real weapons programs being carried out by the government in secret.
The Journal frames its findings as a “stunning new twist in the story of Americaâs cultural obsession with UFOs” but, while the story’s specific anecdotes are certainly new and quite interesting, its broader findings are not, nor are they particularly stunning. Instead, they parrot what many critics of the UFO narrative
have long said
: that the UFO mythos grew out of a disinformation campaign created by shadowy defense officials to obscure more terrestrial secrets about America’s national security community.
Last year,
we wrote a story
with very much the same takeaway, having interviewed one prominent UFO critic, Mark Pilkington, who released a documentary in 2014 arguing that the government used disinformation specialists to lie to Americans and thus hide its covert activities.
Still, the Journal’s investigation offers fresh details about a number of bizarre incidents that will surely tantalize the most avid UFO researchers. In particular, one episode revealed by Kirkpatrick’s investigation involves a UFO sighting at a nuclear bunker that took place in 1967, and seems to show that the government’s disinformation efforts were not merely aimed at members of the public but also its own staff. Robert Salas, a now 84-year-old former Air Force captain, says that his former job was to man the bunker, which would have launched a nuclear strike against the Soviet Union in the event of a nuclear war. One night, Salas says that a “glowing reddish-orange oval” was seen hovering over the front gate of the facility by the building’s guard. Not long afterwards, Salas discovered that the missiles at the facility had mysteriously been disabled.
What had happened? Had aliens managed to disable the base’s nuclear capabilities? The Journal notes that a less supernaturalâif still quite crazyâexplanation for the episode may exist:
Kirkpatrickâs team dug into the story and discovered a terrestrial explanation. The barriers of concrete and steel surrounding Americaâs nuclear missiles were thick enough to give them a chance if hit first by a Soviet strike. But scientists at the time feared the intense storm of electromagnetic waves generated by a nuclear detonation might render the hardware needed to launch a counterstrike unusable.
To test this vulnerability, the Air Force developed an exotic electromagnetic generator that simulated this pulse of disruptive energy without the need to detonate a nuclear weapon. When activated, this device, placed on a portable platform 60 feet above the facility, would gather power until it glowed, sometimes with a blinding orange light. It would then fire a burst of energy that could resemble lightning.
Another intriguing anecdote that is shared in the report involves a bizarre custom that was inflicted upon newly inducted members of highly secretive government programs. Those inductees would be handed a picture of a UFO, Kirkpatrick found:
For decades, certain new commanders of the Air Forceâs most classified programs, as part of their induction briefings, would be handed a piece of paper with a photo of what looked like a flying saucer. The craft was described as an antigravity maneuvering vehicle. The officers were told that the program they were joining, dubbed Yankee Blue, was part of an effort to reverse-engineer the technology on the craft. They were told never to mention it again. Many never learned it was fake. Kirkpatrick found the practice had begun decades before, and appeared to continue still. The defense secretaryâs office sent a memo out across the service in the spring of 2023 ordering the practice to stop immediately, but the damage was done.
Officials who spoke with the newspaper dubbed this practice a “hazing ritual” that spun out of control, but, like most things associated with the UFO phenomenon, it’s easy to find a different interpretation of events. Was this really a “hazing ritual”? Or was it part of an internal disin

data.title: My Mac contacted 63 different Apple owned domains in an hour, while not is use
data.author: rpgbr
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在未使用Mac电脑的情况下，发现其在一个小时内联系了63个不同的苹果域名。尽管作者已使用NextDNS阻止苹果的原生遥测，并禁用了与苹果服务相关的路由，但其M2 MacBook Air（macOS 15.4）仍有25%的DNS查询指向苹果域名。相比之下，作者的2019 Intel MBP在相同DNS设置下只有不到3%的查询涉及苹果域名。文章列出了被联系的苹果域名，包括与推送通知、云服务、iTunes/App Store购买、软件更新、Safari安全浏览等相关的服务。作者已屏蔽了一些苹果服务域名，但仍在尝试减少大科技公司对其生活的渗透。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果系统的后台网络活动及其对用户体验的影响

不同观点：
• **用户期望和系统设计**（al_borland）：用户期望系统在空闲时进行更新和维护，以确保应用和 widget 在打开时已经是最新的，不需要手动刷新。用户希望数据始终是最新的、即时可用的，并能主动提醒重要事项。这种设计主要是为了满足现代用户对即时性和便利性的需求。
  
• **苹果生态系统和网络连接**（SimianSci）：苹果生态系统因其高度集成的服务而受到赞誉，持续的网络连接和客户端轮询是确保大规模设备及时获取更新和通知的必要手段。这种设计是为了应对大规模设备管理中的不可靠连接问题。

• **用户控制和透明度**（al_borland, jitl）：讨论集中在用户对系统后台活动的控制和透明度问题上。一些用户希望有更多控制权，能够自行决定何时进行更新和同步，而不是由系统自动决定。

• **对苹果的批评**（this_user）：一些用户认为苹果已经达到了市场饱和，团队通过改变现有功能和添加不必要的功能来证明其存在价值，这可能会使用户体验变差。

• **安全和隐私问题**（Avamander, mark_l_watson）：有用户担心苹果后台连接的安全性，特别是某些连接未加密，可能被用于设备分析。不过也有用户指出，苹果的大部分数据在传输和存储时都是加密的。

补充讨论：
• **工具和解决方案**（lapcat, thomassmith65）：一些用户提到可以使用工具如 Little Snitch 来检测和阻止不必要的网络连接，或者通过白名单方式管理苹果子域名。

• **对比其他系统**（hoppp, Ardren）：有用户将苹果的做法与其他系统（如 Windows 和 Linux 发行版 Asahi）进行对比，讨论不同系统的网络活动和用户体验。

争议的焦点：
• 用户对后台网络活动的控制权与系统自动维护和更新之间的平衡。
• 苹果生态系统中网络连接的安全性和隐私问题。
• 苹果是否在添加不必要的功能以维持团队存在感和市场地位。

My Mac Contacted 63 Different Apple Owned Domains in One Hour - While Not is Use
During a one hour period today, my computer contacted 63 different Apple
domains while i was not logged on and using it.
I have been trying to minimize to the extent possible the reach of big
tech into my life. A full 25% of the DNS queries from one of my
computers (M2 MBA with macOS 15.4) are to Apple owned domains - even
though my DNS provider (NextDNS) blocks Apple's native telemetry.

blacklisted.

44256338.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在未使用Mac电脑的情况下，发现其在一个小时内联系了63个不同的苹果域名。尽管作者已使用NextDNS阻止苹果的原生遥测，并禁用了与苹果服务相关的路由，但其M2 MacBook Air（macOS 15.4）仍有25%的DNS查询指向苹果域名。相比之下，作者的2019 Intel MBP在相同DNS设置下只有不到3%的查询涉及苹果域名。文章列出了被联系的苹果域名，包括与推送通知、云服务、iTunes/App Store购买、软件更新、Safari安全浏览等相关的服务。作者已屏蔽了一些苹果服务域名，但仍在尝试减少大科技公司对其生活的渗透。
44256338.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果系统的后台网络活动及其对用户体验的影响

不同观点：
• **用户期望和系统设计**（al_borland）：用户期望系统在空闲时进行更新和维护，以确保应用和 widget 在打开时已经是最新的，不需要手动刷新。用户希望数据始终是最新的、即时可用的，并能主动提醒重要事项。这种设计主要是为了满足现代用户对即时性和便利性的需求。
  
• **苹果生态系统和网络连接**（SimianSci）：苹果生态系统因其高度集成的服务而受到赞誉，持续的网络连接和客户端轮询是确保大规模设备及时获取更新和通知的必要手段。这种设计是为了应对大规模设备管理中的不可靠连接问题。

• **用户控制和透明度**（al_borland, jitl）：讨论集中在用户对系统后台活动的控制和透明度问题上。一些用户希望有更多控制权，能够自行决定何时进行更新和同步，而不是由系统自动决定。

• **对苹果的批评**（this_user）：一些用户认为苹果已经达到了市场饱和，团队通过改变现有功能和添加不必要的功能来证明其存在价值，这可能会使用户体验变差。

• **安全和隐私问题**（Avamander, mark_l_watson）：有用户担心苹果后台连接的安全性，特别是某些连接未加密，可能被用于设备分析。不过也有用户指出，苹果的大部分数据在传输和存储时都是加密的。

补充讨论：
• **工具和解决方案**（lapcat, thomassmith65）：一些用户提到可以使用工具如 Little Snitch 来检测和阻止不必要的网络连接，或者通过白名单方式管理苹果子域名。

• **对比其他系统**（hoppp, Ardren）：有用户将苹果的做法与其他系统（如 Windows 和 Linux 发行版 Asahi）进行对比，讨论不同系统的网络活动和用户体验。

争议的焦点：
• 用户对后台网络活动的控制权与系统自动维护和更新之间的平衡。
• 苹果生态系统中网络连接的安全性和隐私问题。
• 苹果是否在添加不必要的功能以维持团队存在感和市场地位。

data.title: Fine-tuning LLMs is a waste of time
data.author: j-wang
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLM）的微调及其替代方法的有效性和应用场景

不同观点：
• [rco8786] 认为模块化方法（如检索增强生成、适配器或提示工程）是将新信息注入模型的更好方式，但存在“中间缺失”问题，即当前方法难以在保持模型性能的同时处理超过上下文窗口大小的专有知识。他提出了一种“上下文压缩”的概念，试图解决这一问题。
• [kouteiheika] 和 [robrenaud] 对 LoRA（低秩适应）进行了技术性分析，指出 LoRA 实际上是通过改变原始权重来实现的，虽然它更高效且适合低端硬件，但本质上仍是微调的一种形式。他们批评了原评论中对 LoRA 的误解。
• [rybosome] 基于实际经验，认为微调在特定任务（如硬件验证）中非常有效，且不介意模型在其他领域的能力受损。他强调微调后的模型可以在一个特定任务上表现得比通用模型更好。
• [kamranjon] 反驳了微调是“浪费时间”的观点，指出微调的优势在于其灵活性和可定制性。他以医学领域的模型为例，说明微调在特定领域的价值。
• [muzani] 分析了微调的演变，指出随着 LLM 的进步和上下文窗口的扩大，RAG（检索增强生成）变得更为可行，微调的需求有所下降，但在某些场景下仍有其价值。
• [simonw] 质疑微调是否常被宣传为知识注入的手段，认为这在实际应用中并不常见。
• [arbfay] 强调微调的风险和成本，建议由经验丰富的工程师主导，并提出使用 PEFT（参数高效微调）技术来降低风险。
• [solresol] 对比了微调和提示工程，认为前者需要更多的资源，但在某些情况下仍具有优势。
• [ankit219] 提供了详细的微调经验，强调了正确的思维模型对结果的影响，并指出了不同方法的优缺点，包括“灾难性遗忘”问题。
• [Mathnerd314] 讨论了 LLM 作为压缩算法的特性，认为微调需要将新数据与原始数据结合才能有效。
• [Havoc] 认为微调更像是“调整”而非“覆盖”，反驳了微调会完全替换模型原有知识的说法。
• [ilaksh] 从实际应用角度出发，认为在复杂业务流程中，使用最智能的通用模型比微调更有效，但在某些具体任务上微调仍有其价值。
• [gdiamos] 分享了微调失败的经验，强调了微调过程中的技术挑战和潜在问题。

补充讨论：
• 微调与提示工程、LoRA、RAG 等方法的对比是讨论的焦点，不同方法在特定场景下的优劣是争议的核心。
• “灾难性遗忘”和模型性能的“损坏”是反对微调的主要论据，但也有观点认为这在特定应用中可以接受。
• 微调的成本和复杂性被多次提及，特别是与提示工程等更轻量级方法的对比。
• 实际应用中的经验和案例为讨论提供了实证支持，如硬件验证和医学领域的成功案例。

data.title: Brazil's Supreme Court makes social media liable for user content
data.author: matheusmoreira
data.article_summary: 巴西最高法院多数法官同意让社交媒体公司对用户发布的非法内容负责，允许对其提起诉讼并处以罚款。目前投票仍在进行中，但只需简单多数即可通过。现行法律仅在社交媒体公司未按法院命令删除有害内容时才追究其责任。尽管该提案即将成为法律，但巴西国会仍可能通过新立法推翻该决定。美国国务卿此前警告可能对参与审查的外国官员实施签证限制。唯一投反对票的法官是Andre Mendonca。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体平台的审核问题以及对非法内容的监管责任

不同观点：
• potato-peeler认为，社交媒体平台的主要问题在于缺乏审核，平台应确保用户的言论文明。他强调，如果人们不会当面说的话，也不应该在网络空间中说。他支持巴西法院的裁决，认为平台需要对社区内的文明负责，特别是对于非法内容，必须加强审核。然而，他也对裁决的执行表示担忧，质疑其实际效果。

• akoboldfrying则更关注该事件的未来发展，推测像Meta和X这样的公司可能会采取极端措施，例如通过IP封锁来应对。他认为这将演变成一场"胆小鬼游戏"（游戏理论中的博弈），即平台可能会以封锁国家作为威胁。此外，他还提到页面上的广告密度问题，认为广告过多影响了阅读体验。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于社交媒体平台应如何在保持用户自由表达权利的同时，有效监管非法内容。potato-peeler强调平台的责任，而akoboldfrying则关注公司可能的应对策略及其潜在后果。

• 另一个值得注意的点是akoboldfrying对广告密度的评论，这虽然不是主要讨论点，但反映了用户对网页体验的关注。

Synopsis
A majority of Brazil's Supreme Court justices support holding social media firms like Meta, X, and Microsoft liable for illegal user posts. The measure, still pending final votes, would allow lawsuits and fines, overturning current law. Congress could still intervene with new legislation to reverse the decision.
TIL Creatives
The majority of justices on Brazil's Supreme Court have agreed to make social media companies liable for
illegal postings
by their users.
Gilmar Mendes
on Wednesday became the sixth of the court's 11 justices to vote to open a path for companies like Meta, X and Microsoft to be sued and pay fines for content published by their users. Voting is ongoing but a simple majority is all that is needed for the measure to pass.
The ruling will come after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned of possible
visa restrictions
against foreign officials allegedly involved in censoring American citizens.
The only dissenting Brazilian justice so far is
Andre Mendonca
and his vote was made public last week.
The social media proposal would become law once voting is finished and the result is published. But Brazil's Congress could still pass another law to reverse the measure.
Live Events
The current legislation states social media companies can only be held responsible in those cases if they do not remove hazardous content after a court order.

data.author: xeonmc
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UI设计的发展、创新与实用性

不同观点：
• [matt_s] 认为Apple已进入成熟公司阶段，创新乏力，特别是在UI设计上，只是对按钮等细节进行微调，缺乏显著增长空间。他还对比了视频游戏与应用UI的视觉设计，指出游戏视觉效果旨在吸引玩家的注意力并展示互动性，而应用UI应简洁、易于操作，尤其是为了满足无障碍标准的需求。

• [uncircle] 认为不同UI风格有其历史演变，提到类似Windows 9x的复古风格，虽然并非创新，但比扁平化设计更具触感和视觉趣味。他以SerenityOS为例，强调三维和触感设计在UI中的价值，认为这种设计更具美学吸引力。

• [qwool] 讨论了Minecraft的界面演变，指出最初的Java版因其简洁和直观受到程序员喜爱，而微软接手后的Bedrock版因过度设计和商业化元素受到批评，导致用户体验下降。

• [pjc50] 提到了Windows 3.0到Aero时代的设计，强调在有限像素预算下，UX设计和无障碍功能的重要性。

• [codingdave] 补充了像素预算对UI设计的影响，指出如果应用没有像素限制，复制受限环境下的设计技巧可能并不合适。

• [0xCE0] 认为Factorio的UI设计是长时间开发和优化的结果，值得借鉴。

• [sandra_vu] 强调字体大小在传达信息层次上的重要性，推荐Stephen Few的书籍以深入了解设计中的视觉扫描性。

• [gizajob] 以戏谑方式建议Apple应将新设计命名为"Liquid Vista"。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于UI设计是否应追求视觉创新还是功能实用性。部分评论者（如matt_s和uncircle）对当前设计的创新性提出质疑，而其他人（如qwool和0xCE0）则通过具体案例讨论了不同设计选择的影响。

• 讨论还涉及历史设计风格的复兴与现代设计需求之间的平衡，以及技术限制对设计决策的影响。

• 无障碍设计在UI设计中的重要性也被多次提及，尤其是在企业环境中应用操作系统UI时。

data.title: IBM now describing its first error-resistant quantum compute system
data.author: donatzsky
data.article_summary: IBM公布了其量子计算新系统的计划，名为Starling，预计2029年推出。该系统能在200个逻辑 qubit上无误执行1亿次操作，并通过捕捉和修正错误实现实用计算，且无法用经典计算方法模拟。IBM还详细描述了通往Starling的中间步骤，包括多个能承载纠错qubit的处理器，逐步转向功能计算单元。IBM将采用低密度奇偶校验（LDPC）代码进行纠错，要求qubit之间具有方形网格连接，并通过多层布线实现长距离耦合。现有“重六边形”配置将被淘汰，新处理器Loon将于今年发布。这项计划标志着IBM从硬件qubit讨论转向功能计算单元的重大转型。

On Tuesday, IBM released its plans for building a system that should push quantum computing into entirely new territory: a system that can both perform useful calculations while catching and fixing errors and be utterly impossible to model using classical computing methods. The hardware, which will be called Starling, is expected to be able to perform 100 million operations without error on a collection of 200 logical qubits. And the company expects to have it available for use in 2029.
Perhaps just as significant, IBM is also committing to a detailed description of the intermediate steps to Starling. These include a number of processors that will be configured to host a collection of error-corrected qubits, essentially forming a functional compute unit. This marks a major transition for the company, as it involves moving away from talking about collections of individual hardware qubits and focusing instead on units of functional computational hardware. If all goes well, it should be possible to build Starling by chaining a sufficient number of these compute units together.
"We're updating [our roadmap] now with a series of deliverables that are very precise," IBM VP Jay Gambetta told Ars, "because we feel that we've now answered basically all the science questions associated with error correction and it's becoming more of a path towards an engineering problem."
New architectures
Error correction on quantum hardware involves entangling a group of qubits in a way that distributes one or more quantum bit values among them and includes additional qubits that can be used to check the state of the system. It can be helpful to think of these as data and measurement qubits. Performing weak quantum measurements on the measurement qubits produces what's called "syndrome data," which can be interpreted to determine whether anything about the data qubits has changed (indicating an error) and how to correct it.
There are lots of potential ways to arrange different combinations of data and measurement qubits for this to work, each referred to as a code. But, as a general rule, the more hardware qubits committed to the code, the more robust it will be to errors, and the more logical qubits that can be distributed among its hardware qubits.
Some quantum hardware, like that based on trapped ions or neutral atoms, is relatively flexible when it comes to hosting error-correction codes. The hardware qubits can be moved around so that any two can be entangled, so it's possible to adopt a huge range of configurations, albeit at the cost of the time spent moving atoms around. IBM's technology is quite different. It relies on qubits made of superconducting electronics laid out on a chip, with entanglement mediated by wiring that runs between qubits. The layout of this wiring is set during the chip's manufacture, and so the chip's design commits it to a limited number of potential error-correction codes.
Unfortunately, this wiring can also enable crosstalk between neighboring qubits, causing them to lose their state. To avoid this, existing IBM processors have their qubits wired in what they term a "heavy hex" configuration, named for its hexagonal arrangements of connections among its qubits. This has worked well to keep the error rate of its hardware down, but it also poses a challenge, since IBM has decided to go with an error-correction code that's incompatible with the heavy hex geometry.
A couple of years back, an IBM team
described a compact error correction code
called a low-density parity check (LDPC). This requires a square grid of nearest-neighbor connections among its qubits, as well as wiring to connect qubits that are relatively distant on the chip. To get its chips and error-correction scheme in sync, IBM has made two key advances. The first is in its chip packaging, which now uses several layers of wiring sitting above the hardware qubits to enable all of the connections needed for the LDPC code.
We'll see that first in a processor called Loon that's on the company's developmental roadmap. "We've already demonstrated these three things: high connectivity, long-range couplers, and couplers that break the plane [of the chip] and connect to other qubits," Gambetta said. "We have to combine them all as a single demonstration showing that all these parts of packaging can be done, and that's what I want to achieve with Loon." Loon will be made public later this year.
On the left, the simple layout of the connections in a current-generation Heron processor. At right, the complicated web of connections that will be present in Loon.
Credit:
IBM

data.title: Agentic Coding Recommendations
data.author: rednafi
data.article_summary:
Armin Ronacher在这篇文章中分享了他对agentic coding的实践和建议。他主要使用Claude Code，并选择便宜的Sonnet模型，以确保输出符合需求。他优化工具使用以提高效率，避免截图和浏览器交互。他的工作流通常是将任务分配给代理，等待其完成，很少干预，因此IDE和AI的作用大大减弱，主要用于最终编辑，甚至重拾了没有AI集成的Vim。

他提到关闭权限检查（使用`claude-yolo`命令）并建议将开发环境移入Docker以控制风险。他还讨论了MCP协议，虽然不常用，但在需要更多工具时会使用。

在语言选择上，Ronacher推荐Go语言用于新后端项目，因其简单的上下文系统、高效的测试缓存、语言的简洁性、结构化接口以及低生态系统变动性。相比之下，Python因其魔法方法和异步处理等问题，不太适合agentic coding。

最后，他提醒技术变化迅速，建议关注有持久力的概念。

Armin Ronacher
's Thoughts and Writings
blog
archive
tags
projects
talks
about
Agentic Coding Recommendations
written on Thursday, June 12, 2025
There is currently an explosion of people sharing their experiences with
agentic coding.  After my last
two
posts
on the topic, I received quite a few
questions about my own practices.  So, here goes nothing.
Preface
For all intents and purposes, here's what I do: I predominently use
Claude Code
with the cheaper
Max subscription for $100 a month
[1]
.  That works well for several
reasons:
I exclusively use the cheaper Sonnet model. It's perfectly adequate for
my needs, and in fact, I prefer its outputs over the more expensive Opus
model.
I optimize my tool usage to be token efficient. I avoid screenshots and
browser interactions wherever possible.  More on that later.
My general workflow involves assigning a job to an agent (which
effectively has full permissions) and then waiting for it to complete the
task.  I rarely interrupt it, unless it's a small task.  Consequently, the
role of the IDE â and the role of AI in the IDE â is greatly diminished;
I mostly use it for final edits.  This approach has even revived my usage
of Vim, which lacks AI integration.
One caveat: I expect this blog post to age very poorly.  The pace of
innovation here is insane; what was true a month ago barely holds true
today.  That's why I'm sticking to concepts I believe have staying power.
If you want to a small session of me working on an Open Source library
with it, I have
a recording you can watch
.
The Basics
I disable all permission checks.  Which basically means I run
claude
--dangerously-skip-permissions
.  More specifically I have an alias
called
claude-yolo
set up.  Now you can call that irresponsible and
there are definitely risks with it, but you can manage those risks with
moving your dev env into docker.  I will however say that if you can watch
it do its thing a bit, it even works surprisingly well without
dockerizing.  YMMV.
MCP.  This is a term you cannot avoid.  It basically is a standardized
protocol to give agents access to more tools.  Honestly: at this point I
barely use it, but I do use it.  The reason I barely use it is because
Claude Code is very capable of just running regular tools.  So MCP for me
is really only needed if I need to give Claude access to something that
finds too hard to use otherwise.  A good example for this is the
playwright-mcp
for
browser automation.  I use it because I haven't found anything better yet.
But for instance when I want my agent to poke around in my database, I
just uses whatever it finds to be available.  In my case it loves to use
psql
and that's more than good enough.
In general I really only start using MCP if the alternative is too
unreliable.  That's because MCP servers themselves are sometimes not super
reliable and they are an extra thing that can go wrong.  Trying to keep
things very simple.  My custom tools are normal scripts that it just runs.
Choice Of Language
I've evaluated agent performance across different languages my workload,
and if you can choose your language, I strongly recommend Go for new
backend projects.  Several factors strongly favor Go:
Context system:
Go provides a capable copy-on-write data bag that
explicitly flows through the code execution path, similar to contextvars
in Python or .NET's execution context.  Its explicit nature greatly
simplifies things for AI agents.  If the agent needs to pass stuff to
any call site, it knows how to do it.
Test caching:
Surprisingly crucial for efficient agentic loops. In
Rust, agents sometimes fail because they misunderstand
cargo test
's
invocation syntax.  In Go, tests run straightforwardly and
incrementally, significantly enhancing the agentic workflow.  It does
not need to figure out which tests to run, go does.
Go is sloppy:
Rob Pike famously described Go as suitable for
developers who aren't equipped to handle a complex language.  Substitute
âdevelopersâ with âagents,â and it perfectly captures why Go's
simplicity benefits agentic coding.
Structural interfaces:
interfaces in Go are structural.  If a type
has the methods an interface expects, then it conforms.  This is
incredibly easy for LLMs to âunderstandâ.  There is very little surprise
for the agent.
Go has low eco-system churn:
Go's entire ecosystem embraces
backwards compatiblity and explicit version moves.  This greatly reduces
the likelihood of AI generating outdated code â starkly contrasting
JavaScript's fast-moving ecosystem for instance.
For comparison, Python â my initial choice â often poses significant
challenges.  Agents struggle with Python's magic (eg: Pytestâs fixture
injection) or complex runtime challenges (eg: wrong event loop when
working with async), frequently producing incorrect code that even the
agentic loop has challenges resolving.  Python also has practical
performance problems.  I don't mean that it writes slow code, i mean that
the agent loop is real

Science
9
Behold! Humanity has captured our first look at the Sun's South Pole
9
Confusingly, the magnetic north and south poles are both down there, where the Solar Orbiter can see them
Iain Thomson
Thu 12 Jun 2025
//
06:30 UTC
Occupants of planet Earth can’t see the Sun’s poles – unless they look at images the Solar Orbiter spacecraft has just sent home.
The Orbiter, a joint NASA/European Space Agency project,
lifted off
in 2020.
The craft helped solar boffins to discover that Sol’s north and south magnetic poles are both on the southern side of the star, as seen from Earth. Scientists don’t know why and ESA rates the current state of our Sun’s magnetic field as "a mess."
Given the Sun’s importance to life on Earth, scientists are keen to know more.
"The Sun is our nearest star, giver of life and potential disruptor of modern space and ground power systems, so it is imperative that we understand how it works and learn to predict its behavior,” said Professor Carole Mundell, ESA's Director of Science in a
statement
.
Mundell hailed the photos of the poles as “the beginning of a new era of solar science.”
Earth-bound observers of the Sun can only see its equatorial regions because of our planet’s steady orbit in a flat elliptic plane. The Solar Orbiter was able to get below the equator, thanks to gravitational assistance from Earth and Venus. The probe has so far performed one Earth flyby and four around Venus, swooping in to use the planets' gravity to adjust its speed without the need for propellant.
South pole of the Sun as seen by Solar Orbiter's Spectral Imaging of the Coronal Environment (SPICE) instrument - Click to enlarge
On February 18, the spacecraft made its
closest approach
yet to Venus, flying just 379km (236 miles) above the surface.
That maneuver put the probe on a course that will eventually see it orbit 17 degrees below the Sun’s equator. The spacecraft captured its first snaps from 15 degrees below the solar equator between March 16 and 17.
Youtube Video
Solar Orbiter is arriving at an interesting time, since the Sun is reaching solar maximum. This is when the north and south magnetic poles reverse positions, which causes the star to belch out more than the usual amount of radiation and charged particles.
This is more than a little worrisome for Earth, given our electronic society's dependence on
datacenters
, satellites, and other kit solar emissions could damage. We
dodged a bullet
in 2012 when a coronal mass ejection powerful enough to fry electronics on Earth's surface missed us
by a whisker
.
Our first glimpse of the hidden poles. Source: ESA
By using its Polarimetric and Helioseismic Imager (PHI), Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUI), and the Spectral Imaging of the Coronal Environment (SPICE) instrument, the Solar Orbiter spacecraft scanned the Sun to see how these magnetic changes affect such solar outbursts.
The Sun’s poles are literally terra incognita
"How exactly this build-up occurs is still not fully understood, so Solar Orbiter has reached high latitudes at just the right time to follow the whole process from its unique and advantageous perspective," commented Professor Sami Solanki, leader of the PHI instrument team from the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research in Germany.
"We didn’t know what exactly to expect from these first observations – the Sun’s poles are literally terra incognita."
Sun's magnetic mystery solved by ESA NASA Solar Orbiter

Parker Solar Probe sends a "Still Alive" tone back to Earth
Solar Orbiter was also able to examine the substance of the Sun's outer shell by analyzing the composition of its upper atmosphere using the Spectral Imaging of the Coronal Environment (SPICE) spectrograph. Data from that instrument should give us a better understanding of how and why the Sun spews material into space by clocking the speed of ejected star-stuff based on variations in observed color, the so-called "Doppler measurement".
“Doppler measurements of solar wind setting off from the Sun by current and past space missions have been hampered by the grazing view of the solar poles. Measurements from high latitudes, now possible with Solar Orbiter, will be a revolution in solar physics,” predicted SPICE team leader, Frédéric Auchère from the University of Paris-Saclay (France).
NASA and ESA have collaborated before on solar research, firing off the Ulysses probe in 1990, which reached the Sun thanks to a gravitational assist from Jupiter. It managed to take readings on the solar magnetic fields, although it didn't carry a camera. The 17-year mission involved three flybys and produced data that informed the Solar Orbiter mission.
The Solar Orbiter will make
four more
close encounters with Venus to adjust its course, with the next to take place on Christmas Eve 2026. It should reach a pole-to-pole

data.title: Minister of International Trade says Canada should apply for EU
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 加拿大国际贸易部长曼德·西杜提出，加拿大应寻求加入欧盟以实现贸易多元化，摆脱对美国的依赖。他指出，法国海外领地圣皮埃尔和密克隆群岛距纽芬兰仅19公里，从地理上使加拿大更接近欧洲。此言论令当地居民和加拿大人感到惊讶，因为许多人都不知道圣皮埃尔和密克隆是法国领土。西杜还幽默地提到加拿大与丹麦在汉斯岛的陆地边界，并暗示可能加入南美的Mercosur或非洲联盟。尽管其提议引发质疑，西杜表示将探索其他贸易集团加入可能性。法国外交部对此表示意外，称未意识到圣皮埃尔和密克隆不属加拿大。

OTTAWA – Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu has said
Canada
should pursue European
Union
membership as part of the government’s plan to diversify trade away from the United States.
When asked by reporters about the logistics of Canada joining the
European Union
when they are across the Atlantic Ocean, Sidhu replied that the French territory of
Saint Pierre and Miquelon
is only nineteen kilometres off the coast of
Newfoundland
, a fact which shocked both Canadians and residents of the French islands.
“I had no idea we were even part of
France
!” said Antoine Gascón, a resident of the capital, Saint Pierre. “We use Canadian dollars, I have a Canadian bank account, I can see Newfoundland from my back porch, what do you mean this is France?”
A 2022 poll of Canadians found that only tenth graders who visited the islands on a
school
field trip were aware that Saint Pierre and Miquelon were part of France.
“Technically, this makes us closer to Europe than the island of Great
Britain
is,” Sidhu noted hopefully said to reporters. “We also have a land border with Denmark on Hans Island. Hint hint.”
However, reporters continued to question the Minister on the logistics of Canada joining a European-based bloc. “If Australia is allowed to compete in Eurovision, surely we can get membership in the European Union?” Sidhu stated, noting that the surviving members of Rush were ready to compose a competitive pop song at a moment’s notice.
Sidhu also clarified that he is looking at other trading blocs for Canada to try and join. “Since French Guiana is in South
America
, that basically puts us right next to Brazil, so why don’t we also join Merocsur? Or how about the African Union? France still has islands between Mozambique and Madagascar, so we’re also right next door! That’s a good enough reason to join, right?”
When asked about the subject, France’s foreign affairs ministry said: “Wait, Saint Pierre and Miquelon aren’t already part of Canada?”

data.title: Why do Bedouins wear black robes in hot deserts? (1980)
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 文章研究了为何贝都因人在炎热沙漠中穿着黑色长袍。传统上，人们可能认为白色衣物更能反射阳光，减少热量吸收，但研究发现，穿着黑色长袍的贝都因人和穿着白色长袍的人在沙漠中吸收的热量相同。黑色长袍额外吸收的热量在到达皮肤之前就已经散失。实验表明，在风速大于3米/秒的情况下，黑色衣物下的热流并没有比白色衣物更多。这解释了为何贝都因人在沙漠中选择穿黑色长袍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：服饰颜色与温度调节的关系以及引用神话人物作为科学依据的适当性

不同观点：
• [mikhailfranco的观点] 认为在阿拉伯地区，女性穿黑色服饰是为了在室内更好地散热，而男性穿白色服饰是为了在户外更好地反射阳光。这种解释基于个人在阿拉伯地区的有限观察和直觉。

• [SapporoChris的观点] 对引用神话人物如摩西作为科学论文的开篇引用表示质疑，认为这并不能增强可信度。特别指出，大多数学者认为圣经中的摩西是一个传奇人物，从而质疑引用此类人物来讨论历史或科学问题的适当性。

补充讨论：
• mikhailfranco的评论更多基于个人经验和观察，提出了关于服饰颜色在不同环境下调节体温的假设。虽然没有提供科学数据支持，但这种解释具有一定的直觉性和实践性。

• SapporoChris的评论集中在学术严谨性上，强调科学论文应基于可验证的事实和证据，而不是神话或传说。通过引用维基百科上关于摩西的学术观点，SapporoChris指出引用神话人物可能削弱论文的科学可信度。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于引用神话人物作为科学依据的适当性以及服饰颜色与温度调节关系的经验性解释的可信度。SapporoChris认为科学应与神话和传说区分开来，而mikhailfranco的经验性观察虽然直观，但缺乏科学验证。

44255243.article_content:
Abstract
Survival in hot deserts has always posed a problem for man; Moses had to solve it in order to lead the children of Israel through the wilderness of the Sinai—a formidable hot desert. It seems likely that the present inhabitants of the Sinai, the Bedouins, would have optimised their solutions for desert survival during their long tenure in this desert Yet, one may have doubts on first encountering Bedouins wearing black robes and herding black goats. We have therefore investigated whether black robes help the Bedouins to minimise solar heat loads in a hot desert. This seemed possible because experiments have shown that white hair on cattle
1,2
and white feathers on pigeons
3
permit greater penetration of short-wave radiation to the skin than black. In fact, more heat flowed inward through white pigeon plumage than through black when both were exposed to simulated solar radiation at wind speeds greater than 3 m s
−1
(ref. 3). We report here that the amount of heat gained by a Bedouin exposed to the hot desert is the same whether he wears a black or a white robe. The additional heat absorbed by the black robe was lost before it reached the skin.
